title: O and N
summary: Two new keys: O and N. The finger goes out, presses, and comes back.
intro: Two new keys in this lesson: O and N. They belong to your left ring finger and your right ring finger. The movement is always the same — out, press, back — and the way back is the part being trained, because a finger left out of place spoils the next letter.
congrats: Two more keys under your fingers. If O and N already come without searching, the lesson has done its job.

screens.text: This key belongs to your left ring finger. Find it without looking, press it once, and let the finger return. The way back matters as much as the press.
Only O and what you already know. Slowly, and bring the finger back to the home row after every press.
screens.content:
euo h eu
o o oo
ooo

screens.text: This key belongs to your right ring finger. Find it without looking, press it once, and let the finger return. The way back matters as much as the press.
Only N and what you already know. Slowly, and bring the finger back to the home row after every press.
screens.content:
ooo nnnn
ononon nonono
on no

screens.text: Short groups, one after another. Keep going to the end even if you miss one.
The new keys mixed with the old ones, which is how they will turn up inside words.
screens.content:
uhno huon
tnu oeh tn
uo ou uouo

screens.text: Real words with the new keys. Type each word in one go, not letter by letter.
screens.content:
on to tooth one
onto tooth too ten
ten tone out hot

screens.text: A burst of short words with the new keys in them.
Now the weight is on O, the one you have pressed least.
screens.content:
not onto then hot
hunt note on to
tone too ten he

screens.text: Back to patterns for a moment, to check that the fingers still find their way home.
screens.content:
no on
ohu ne oh
on no onon

screens.text: Everything you have, mixed together. Notice how many words already come without thinking.
screens.content:
then out too the
out on then tooth
no ten hot on
